notes.lines: Every line on this map is a 2020 census block's, generalised by at most 1.5 metres and set on a grid of 0.00001 degree (about a metre); city, town and village limits are the Census Bureau's 2025 lines. A point within a few metres of a line can fall on either side of it.
notes.precincts: Florida law (section 101.001(3)(c)) requires every precinct to be made of whole census blocks, so each precinct here is rebuilt from blocks. In 20 counties (Alachua County, Baker County, Bay County, Broward County, Hillsborough County, Leon County, Martin County, Miami-Dade County, Nassau County, Okaloosa County, Orange County, Osceola County, Palm Beach County, Pinellas County, St. Lucie County, Santa Rosa County, Sarasota County, Seminole County, Sumter County, Volusia County) the precincts are the county's current precincts, from the county's own published map: each block is put in the precinct holding it. In every other county a precinct is the voting district the county reported for the 2020 census; many counties have redrawn or renumbered their precincts since. Wherever a House, Senate, congressional or commission line crosses a precinct it is cut, and each piece is named as a part; every piece carries the districts of its own blocks, so the districts at a point are exact for House, Senate and Congress even where the county's map and a district line disagree about a block (a small piece along a line most often marks such a disagreement). The same law lets a precinct follow a city's newer limits, which can cut a block; a precinct of the county's map smaller than the blocks it lies in is not drawn (precinct_lines lists them), and a point in one is given the precinct holding the rest of its block. The county's Supervisor of Elections is the authority on which precinct an address is in.
notes.congressional: The congressional districts are plan EOGPCRP2026, enacted on May 4, 2026 and in force for 2026 (a challenge is pending in state court). Every block is placed by the official block equivalency file, so a precinct's district is exact; no reader is placed by the 2024 lines. A county's own layer is never read for its congressional district: Orange County's 2026 sub-precinct layer, read here only for the county commission districts, still gives the 2022 districts in its congressional field (checked on 2026-10-17: 386 of its 389 pieces agree with the 2022 plan, 267 with EOGPCRP2026).
notes.legislative: House and Senate districts are the 2022 plans (H000H8013, S027S8058), placed block by block from EDR's files; the Census Bureau's 2024 files agree on every block.
notes.judicial: The 20 judicial circuits are whole counties (section 26.021); circuit judges, state attorneys and public defenders are elected by the circuit. The six appellate districts are groups of circuits (sections 35.02 to 35.044): dca names a precinct's, and an appellate judge's retention vote is on the ballots of that district. County court judges are elected by the whole county.
notes.places: Cities, towns and villages are the Census Bureau's 2025 places. A precinct lying wholly in one names it (mcd); one that reaches into several lists them (mcd_all, with each one's share of the precinct's area). The mcd layer answers for a point.
notes.commissioners: Florida's county commissioners are elected by the whole county unless the county's voters chose single-member districts. supervisor_plans gives, for each county, which of its 2026 seats were elected at large and which by district, read from which precincts reported each district's contest in the Division of Elections' official results (analysis). Commission districts are drawn for Alachua County, Brevard County, Broward County, Clay County, Collier County, Escambia County, Hendry County, Hillsborough County, Leon County, Manatee County, Miami-Dade County, Orange County, Osceola County, Palm Beach County, Pinellas County, Sarasota County, Volusia County, from the county's own lines. Every other contest elected by district is listed under check, with the reason.
notes.school: Each county is one school district (Florida Constitution, Article IX, section 4), so a school district's shape is its county's. School board members are elected from residence districts the files do not draw.
notes.special_districts: Community development, fire, mosquito control, water control, hospital, port, airport, library, utility and soil and water conservation districts are not drawn: no official file of their boundaries that a script may read was found. Their contests are listed under check.
notes.authority: For which precinct an address votes in, and where, the county's Supervisor of Elections and the Division of Elections' voter lookup are the authority.
notes.precinct_ids: A precinct's id is its county's five digits, a full stop and the precinct's number: the county's own where its current precincts are read (12086.101), else the Census Bureau's 2020 voting district code (12001.000046); a precinct cut by a district line has .p and the piece's number after it.
